text:
sam: Heads up — multiple customer tickets about 503s starting ~10:12 UTC after the canary push. Tickets attached: #4321, #4322. Grafana spike on api-gateway latency.
deploy-bot: Deployment event: service=redwood-api env=prod rollout=canary user=raj config_change=enable_prefetch_v2=true commit=7f3a9b
sre-oncall: I can confirm a 5xx spike across gateway frontends and increased backend 502/503. Error rate up ~12% in last 5m. Traces show requests timing out waiting on model-proxy.
support-alex: Customers reporting immediate 503s when hitting /v1/generate, some see 504s. One customer gave curl output:
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  HTTP/2 503
  content-type: application/json
  {"error":"gateway_error","message":"upstream failure: model-proxy timed out"}
sam: Any quick rollback plan? Can we abort canary and re-route traffic to previous variant?
raj: Pushing rollback now. Noted that canary flipped `enable_prefetch_v2` and `route_by_prefetch` together. We intended only prefetch toggle, but route flag propagated to canary-targetset by mistake (config scoping bug).
olivia-pm: That matches customer repro — some requests were routed to a path without kv-cache warmup, causing timeouts under load.
infra-mike: Rolling back canary via:
  deployctl rollback --service redwood-api --to-tag=release-2026-03-16 --scope=canary
  kubectl -n prod set env deployment/redwood-api ENABLE_PREFETCH_V2=false
sre-oncall: Also disabling canary weight and draining nodes: set traffic-slice canary=0. Observed immediate drop in 5xx within 2m after reducing weight on a test instance. Canary had ~30% of traffic due to autoscale rule.
support-alex: Notifying affected customers and tagging support ticket with mitigation steps. Will request logs from a customer who repros.
raj: Root cause preliminary: config service published flags with wrong selector label (label:route=canary-target vs route=canary). The selector mismatch allowed the routing config to leak to unrelated router groups. Working on a fix for config-service selector resolution.
sre-oncall: For postmortem, capture: deploy author, exact commits, config-service version, canary weight, and traffic slices. We should add a guard in rollout pipeline to disallow simultaneous routing and prefetch toggles.
olivia-pm: Agreed. Also need a playbook entry: when canary 5xx spike, immediately set canary weight=0, then rollback config key, then drain. We missed a quick disable button in console.
infra-mike: Quick log snippet from model-proxy showing connection queue saturation:
  2026-03-16T10:13:21Z ERROR proxy::upstream ConnectionTimeout { peer: "10.12.8.45:31415", waited_ms: 5000 }
  2026-03-16T10:13:21Z WARN  prefetch::warmup Cache miss for session abc123, kicked async warmup
raj: I'll follow up with a patch to config-service to enforce atomic flag groups and add a dry-run validation for selector labels.
sam: Thanks — once rollback stabilizes, let's schedule a triage at 11:30 to agree on mitigations and customer comms. @support-alex, prioritize customers with SLA clauses.
support-alex: On it. Sending status update to affected accounts now. :email:
sre-oncall: Monitoring — will post when error rate back to baseline. Current error rate trending down after rollback to 3% -> 0.8% in 6m.
sam: Good. If anything spikes again ping all-hands channel. :thumbsup:
